claim: Automatminer Express preset achieves the best performance on 8 of 13 tasks in the Matbench benchmark.
claim: Automatminer source code and pre-processed Matbench tasks are open source and available online.
claim: Automatminer's auto-generated models outperform or equal the Random Forest model across all Matbench tasks except predicting formation energies across the Materials Project.

claim: Descriptor-based Automatminer and RF models have lower errors on small datasets but their improvement rates are shallower, with AutoML's advantage over conventional techniques narrowing as sample count increases and essentially lost near 10^5 samples.

claim: For small datasets (<10^4 samples), inexpensive Automatminer presets (~1-5 minute training) retain the bulk of performance compared to expensive presets (24h+ training), with Express retaining 95% or more of the accuracy of more expensive presets at less than 50% of the computational cost on data-scarce tasks.

claim: AFLOW calculations follow a standardized sequential workflow: RELAX1 → RELAX2 → STATIC → BANDS for materials in the Elements, ICSD, and Heusler databases.
claim: AFLOW can automatically construct convex hulls for binary alloy systems at zero temperature using formation enthalpies from DFT calculations.
claim: AFLOW can predict alloy miscibility using Miedema and Hume-Rothery mixing rules.
claim: AFLOW provides a standardized definition of Brillouin-zone integration paths for all 14 Bravais lattices, filling a gap in the literature.
claim: AFLOW reproduces experimental phonon dispersion curves for face-centered cubic Rhodium, showing excellent agreement with measured data.

claim: AFLOW’s cage-finding algorithm identifies interstitial sites via a topological method, finding 14 cages (6 octahedral, 8 tetrahedral) that reduce to 5 symmetrically inequivalent positions, with radii of 2.2225 Å (octahedral) and 1.9248 Å (tetrahedral).
claim: BANDS calculations use 128 k-points per segment for single element structures and 20 k-points for compounds along high-symmetry paths.

claim: Default NKPPRA values for non-BANDS calculations vary by database: Binary Alloy uses 6000 for RELAX, Heusler uses 10000 for STATIC and 6000 for RELAX, and ICSD uses 10000 for STATIC and 8000 for RELAX.

claim: Electronic convergence criteria are δEelec = 10-5 eV and ionic convergence criteria are δEion = 10-4 eV for Elements database entries, while all other databases use δEelec = 10-3 eV and δEion = 10-2 eV.

claim: Future development plans include adding calculations of surface energies, elastic constants, point defects, finite-temperature properties, and implementing a two-way ‘calculations-on-demand’ feature for user-submitted compounds.
claim: Hybrid functional calculations scale approximately as O(N^2.5) for small systems and linearly beyond ~15 Å (HSE06) or ~100 Å (PBE0), whereas standard GGA calculations scale as O(N^3).

claim: The AFLOW standard enables reproducible high-throughput DFT calculations through standardized parameter sets for k-point density, energy cut-offs, exchange-correlation functionals, pseudopotentials, DFT+U parameters, and convergence criteria.
claim: The AFLOWLIB data is accessible through a REST-API for standardized data exchange.
claim: The AFLOWLIB repository contains calculated properties of over 625,000 materials across Binary Alloy Project, Electronic Structure database, Heusler database, and Elements database.

claim: The Materials Project aims to reduce the typical 10-20 year timeline for advanced material development by providing large-scale accurate information, thereby accelerating discovery for clean energy, electronics, and other sectors.

claim: A bulk ZnO HSE06 calculation (8×8×6 k-point mesh, 400 eV cutoff) takes approximately 5 hours on 8 CPUs, while the equivalent GGA/PBE+U calculation finishes in less than a minute.
claim: AFLOW can automatically calculate a wide suite of physical observables across a large database of structures with minimal human intervention.
claim: AFLOW can automatically create nanoparticle structures of arbitrary radius and separation, enabling high-throughput nanoparticle studies.
claim: AFLOW can automatically generate high-index surface slabs for complex multicomponent compounds, demonstrated for (001), (110) and (111) slabs of an fcc L10 binary.

claim: AFLOW detects most calculation failures, automatically corrects input parameters, restarts calculations, and can run as a Unix daemon to generate, run, correct, and converge many DFT jobs per day, yielding higher throughput than manual management.
claim: AFLOW implements DFT+U using the Dudarev formalism with default Ueff values for a wide range of elements.
claim: Automated validation checks compare calculated oxidation states, cell volumes, and bond lengths against experimental data and flag outliers for user review.
claim: Class-specific computational methodologies and reference reactions are applied for solid-gas, d-block oxide, and dissolved-ion systems to improve agreement with experimental data.
claim: DFT+U corrections are applied to the entire ICSD database and certain Heusler database entries containing O, S, Se, and F elements, but not to the Binary Alloy database.

claim: Following the AFLOW standard enables materials science researchers to reproduce AFLOWLIB consortium results and make direct comparisons of properties between different materials for identifying trends and formulating design rules.

claim: High-throughput computational screening through the Materials Project has screened tens of thousands of compounds and identified promising candidates for solar water splitting, photovoltaics, topological insulators, scintillators, CO2 capture, piezoelectrics, thermoelectrics, catalysis, hydrogen storage, and Li-ion batteries, with experimental hits reported in several areas.

claim: Specific Ueff parameters are defined for d-block elements (Table 4) and U, J parameters for f-block elements (Table 5) to correct self-interaction error in DFT+U calculations, with values ranging from 1.9 eV (In) to 7.5 eV (Zn).
claim: The AFLOW database currently contains approximately 400 experimental prototype structures and several million bcc/fcc/hcp-derived superstructures.
claim: The PBE functional combined with PAW potentials is the default exchange-correlation functional and potential combination for ICSD, Binary Alloy, and Heusler databases.

claim: The distribution of chromium coordination environments in oxides derived from the database matches known chemical principles: Cr6+ prefers tetrahedral (4-fold) coordination, while Cr3+ prefers octahedral (6-fold) coordination.

claim: The first RELAX calculation is performed in collinear spin-polarized fashion with initial magnetic moments set to 1.0 μB per atom, and spin polarization is turned off in subsequent calculations if magnetization is below 0.025 μB/atom.

claim: The open-source software infrastructure of the Materials Project, including pymatgen, has attracted more than 100 active collaborators worldwide and incorporates community contributions such as FEFF and ABINIT support.

claim: The workflow software FireWorks together with the custodian job-management tool automatically manages high-throughput DFT calculations, self-heals failed runs, and applies material-type-specific workflows.
claim: Tuning the exact-exchange fraction α to 0.375 in HSE06 brings the calculated ZnO band gap into agreement with experiment.
